speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me if your symptoms started after any recent neck injury or prolonged awkward positioning? Also, does the pain radiate specifically down your arm into your fingers, and which fingers are affected?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Radiculopathy. Given the chronic progression, bilateral hand weakness, and significant risk factors like diabetes and age, immediate MRI of the cervical spine is required to evaluate for spinal cord compression and plan for potential surgical intervention.
